Our Craft

From bottle to bedside table

The bottle is the signature. Each one is cut, finished, and inspected by hand before a single drop of wax goes in — so the candle looks as good unlit as it smells lit.

1

Cut & smooth

Glass bottles are hand-cut and the edge is sanded and polished until it's smooth to the touch.

2

Pour in small batches

Soy wax is blended with fragrance and hand-poured, so scent stays true from first light to last.

3

Cure & finish

Candles cure before they ship, for a stronger, cleaner scent throw — then they're ready to gift or keep.

Our Story

Made in Atlanta, by hand

Lit Up Candle Co. was founded by Stacey Fish in Atlanta on a simple idea: a candle should be beautiful before you ever light it. That meant rethinking the vessel itself — hand-cut bottles, each with its own character — and filling them with small-batch soy wax poured with care.

Today the shop still does it the slow way: cut, pour, cure, and finish — one small batch at a time — plus custom orders for the moments people want to remember.

— Stacey Fish, Founder

Questions? Email connect@litupcandleco.com or ask the assistant anytime.

Good to know

Questions shoppers ask most

How long do the candles burn?

In this demo, signature candles are listed at roughly 45–55 hours. Trim the wick to about ¼″ before each burn and let the wax melt edge-to-edge the first time for the cleanest burn. Final specs to be confirmed by the shop.

Are the candles really in bottles?

Yes — that's the signature. Each vessel starts as a glass bottle, hand-cut and smoothed, then filled with soy wax. Because they're handmade, slight variations are part of the charm.

Do you take custom or bulk orders?

Yes — weddings, events, corporate gifts, and wholesale. Ask the assistant about custom orders and it will outline options and how to reach Stacey to start yours.

What wax do you use?

100% soy wax, hand-poured in small batches in Atlanta. Soy burns slower and cleaner than paraffin and holds fragrance well through the life of the candle.
